q: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the ____ (or) heat capacity of the object.
e: Thermal capacity measures the total heat needed for a 1-degree temperature change in an object.

q: The thermal capacity of an object is given by the formula $C =$ ____.
e: Thermal capacity is the ratio of thermal energy added to the resulting temperature change.

q: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is ____ ($J K^{-1}$).
e: The SI unit for thermal capacity is joules per kelvin.

q: The thermal capacity of an object depends on ____ and a type of the material it is made of.
e: Thermal capacity is an extensive property, meaning it scales with the object's mass.

q: Water has a relatively ____ thermal capacity.
e: Water can absorb a large amount of heat with only a small change in temperature.

q: Because of high thermal capacity, water is used to ____ engines.
e: Water's ability to absorb large amounts of heat makes it an effective coolant.

q: Suppose that the internal energy of ____ of a substance changes by $\Delta Q$ due to the temperature change $\Delta T$.
e: Molar thermal capacity is defined based on a quantity of one mole of the substance.

q: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is ____.
e: Molar thermal capacity standardizes heat capacity to a per-mole basis.

q: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is ____ ($J mol^{-1}K^{-1}$).
e: The SI unit for molar thermal capacity is joules per mole per kelvin.
